title: Nine-region correction uncertainty can reverse the 1982-2022 DOISST feedback change at a fixed global mean
abstract: We tested whether spatial uncertainty in a DOISST step correction changes its inferred radiative effect when the global mean correction stays fixed. We used published step maps and five model Green's functions over ice-free ocean at 60 S to 60 N. Regional scales range from 0.5 to 1, with a mean correction equal to common scaling by 0.75. Exact linear programs give five-model mean raw-minus-corrected feedback bounds of -0.020 to +0.141 W m-2 K-1 for the in situ fit and -0.008 to +0.189 for the CCI fit in 1982-2022. A five-function smooth field keeps this long-period effect positive, but reduces its lower bound to +0.001 or +0.015. Both spatial tests permit both signs in 2001-2022. Independent vertex enumeration confirms the nine-region bounds. The result shows which sign claims require spatial error assumptions. It does not show that a sign reversal occurred. The scale ranges are sensitivity assumptions, not confidence limits, and no new SST observations constrain them.

display.caption: Fixed global mean correction with different spatial scales. Thick lines show nine-region bounds. Thin lines show box bounds. Dots use one common scale. These are sensitivity bounds, not confidence intervals.
